ops.anchor: What skills does a number 10 need?
ops.html:
Is the number 10 role disappearing?

No, but it has moved. The classic central 10 who waits for the ball and doesn't defend is rarer, because modern teams press hard and squeeze the space between the lines. The job itself, receiving between the lines and making the final pass, now gets done by free 8s, false 9s and inverted wingers.

  • 4-2-3-1 and 4-3-1-2: the central 10 still exists, but he is expected to press and block the lane into their holding midfielder.
  • 4-3-3: two 8s take turns in the left and right half-spaces, the area between the full-back and center back.
  • False 9: the striker drops into the 10 space and pulls a center back out with him.
  • Inverted wingers: they cut inside into the same zone from the outside.

What this means for you: if you see yourself as a 10, learn to do the 10's job from more than one starting spot, as an 8 and off one wing. Coaches pick players who can create from several positions and who work without the ball.

ops.anchor: knowing what is behind you before the ball arrives (see how to scan in soccer).
ops.html:
Are you a number 10? A quick self-check

  • You want the ball in tight spaces, with defenders close, rather than out wide.
  • You look for a pass before you look for a dribble.
  • You can receive and play with either foot without stopping the ball.
  • You are happy to press and block lanes when your team loses the ball.
  • You can shoot from the edge of the box when the defense backs off.

Four or five yeses: the 10 role suits you. Two or three: try the free 8 role first, which asks for the same skills with more running.

faq_add.a: Trequartista is Italian for a three-quarter player: a number 10 who plays between midfield and attack with freedom to roam and few defensive jobs. Totti and Baggio are classic examples. Modern coaches rarely give a player that much freedom without the ball.

faq_add.q: What is the difference between a number 10 and a false 9?
faq_add.a: A number 10 starts in midfield, behind the striker, and moves up into the space between the lines. A false 9 starts as the striker and drops back into that same space, pulling a center back out of position. Same zone, different starting point.

faq_add.q: Can a winger play as a number 10?
faq_add.a: Yes, and many do. Inverted wingers already receive in the half-space and cut inside, which is close to the 10's job. The big change is that pressure comes from all sides instead of one, so scanning before you receive matters even more.
